clue.text: Hazard for driver is pond collapsing in Sandwich

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the sandwich's letters

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich

indicators.note: something collapsing falls into a heap, so the letters of 'is pond' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collapsing pond inside a sandwich is a peril for a motorist, an absurd picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwich' looks like the Kent town but is the bacon, lettuce and tomato kind; 'collapsing' rearranges the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A region a motorist cannot see in the mirrors is a well-known road danger.

clue.text: Surgeon saving man without skeleton?

indicators.note: saving here means holding on to, so one piece keeps the other within it

parts.note: Bones is the nickname of Dr McCoy, ship's surgeon in Star Trek; also short for sawbones
Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: A surgeon rescuing a man who seems to have lost his skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means holding inside. The question mark flags the literal reading of a word usually meaning filleted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any bones is literally lacking a skeleton, a whimsical reading of the cookery term for filleted.

clue.text: Northerner's short stay in Paris hotel?

indicators.note: cut short, so a pair of the repeated letters where the two pieces meet is dropped

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
a night's stay is une nuit in French

explanation.surface: A northern visitor spends a brief night in a hotel in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops two of the three Ns from INNNUIT. The setter's pun is that the answer sounds like 'une nuit', one night in French; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous peoples of Arctic Canada and Greenland live about as far north as anyone.

clue.text: Waiter had slung out relatives

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A waiter has thrown some relatives out of the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that all the letters of WAITER HAD SLUNG are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives of one's sons are relations by marriage.

clue.text: Transport from local with no drink served up

parts.note: a local is a pub, and PH is the abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means written upwards, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A pub turns out to have no drink to serve, so you leave by some vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' makes AETON in this down clue. A local in Britain is one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage is a means of getting about.

clue.text: Rejected expertise about hurt body part

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
rejected in a down clue means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: art is skill or expertise
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: Someone's skill is rejected because of an injured part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' makes TRA, and 'about' wraps it round the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the tube in the neck carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: One has large bill, heading for insolvency again

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: Someone with a huge bill to pay is headed for bankruptcy once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes the I of insolvency. 'bill' is a beak, not an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird is known for its long down-curved beak.

clue.text: Last drink? Cheers!

parts.note: the bottom is the last or lowest place
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Calling the last round of drinks, with a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole clue as one toast; in fact the definition is only 'Cheers!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts spoken while raising glasses before drinking.

clue.text: Make sure to keep vicious dog properly restrained

indicators.note: to keep here means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to see to it is to make sure
a cur is a snappish mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Advice to check that a dangerous dog is safely tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make sure' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; 'to keep' means to hold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened tightly and safely is firmly held in place.

clue.text: Demand huge amount to power planet?

parts.note: to charge a battery is to power it
the Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: Asking a fortune to supply electricity to the whole world.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the wordplay half reads the idiom literally, as energising the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for asking an exorbitant price or overcharging.

clue.text: Westbound vessel ships gold in 21 location

indicators.note: ships here means carries aboard, so one piece holds the other
in an across clue westbound runs right to left, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A vessel heading west carries a cargo of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westbound' makes NRU and 'ships' means carries inside. The 21 refers to the answer at 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny Pacific island republic lies in the region spanning Australasia and the Pacific islands.

clue.text: Note way it makes return in City without interest

parts.note: A is a musical note
a path is a way

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: making a return means going back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A banker's memo: the money comes back to the City with no interest paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' suggests money but means concern; 'makes return' makes TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling no enthusiasm or concern is lacking any curiosity or care.

clue.text: Old thong is discarded in rude athletics

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so these letters are removed from the pool
rude here means rough or unrefined, so the remaining letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An old sandal strap is thrown aside during some rough-and-ready sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of ATHLETICS to leave ATHLETC, which 'rude' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a leather strap or lace fastening a shoe.

clue.text: Hotel bower provides shelter

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an arbour is a leafy bower

explanation.surface: A hotel's garden bower gives guests a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven or place of refuge, especially for ships.

clue.text: Ascend as viper making move in game

indicators.note: to move the letters is to shift them into a new order

explanation.surface: A snake climbing up as a move in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges all of ASCEND AS VIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic 1978 arcade video title about shooting descending aliens.

clue.text: Harshness in wind over town 100 must flee

parts.note: Auster is the south wind in Latin poetry

indicators.note: fleeing means leaving, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a city is a large town
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Severe weather: a gale over a town drives a hundred people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must flee' removes C from CITY to leave ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity or sternness, also strict economy.

clue.text: Reactionaries one used to give protection on train?

definitions.text: one used to give protection on train?
definitions.meaning: a former railway guard, someone who once looked after a train

explanation.surface: Conservatives once did security work on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-standing, change-resistant members of a group, and literally an elderly or former train guard.

clue.text: Church in Palestine is unusual religious venue

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church in the Holy Land is an unusual place to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes SISTINEAPEL from the fodder, split to take the church inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal chapel in the Vatican, famous for Michelangelo's ceiling.

clue.text: Setter's getting on making pictures

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so setter's is I'm, I am
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is growing old while drawing pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing visual representations, as in medical scanning.

clue.text: Agreement achieved with three tens, minus tips

indicators.note: tips are the ends of a word, so the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: the word ten written three times

explanation.surface: A deal reached on thirty, less some service charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus tips' drops the outer T and N from TENTENTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Millions root for socialist craftsman

parts.note: orris is the fragrant root of an iris

explanation.surface: Millions of people cheer on a left-wing artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris was the Arts and Crafts designer who was also a committed socialist.

clue.text: Sea current advanced in Orwellian superstate

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
I is the physics symbol for electric current
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A sea current pushed forward in an Orwell-style state.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three warring superpowers in Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Chinese food or bite taken outside theatre

indicators.note: one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: tang is a sharp bite of flavour
rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A Chinese takeaway, or a snack eaten outside the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bite' is a sharp flavour, not a mouthful; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea cucumber, a delicacy dried and used in Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Tool cutting into metal is so long

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, going inside it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a stamping or cutting tool

explanation.surface: A tool cuts into metal and it takes a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length; it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye, from the French for 'to God'.

clue.text: Sport one associates with Land's End

parts.note: RU is rugby union
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a land

explanation.surface: A sport someone links with the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall in England; here 's means 'is' and 'End' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter destruction or downfall is a ruinous end.

clue.text: Indian recipe author read out

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the word's sound gives the letters

parts.note: an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A cookbook writer reads an Indian recipe to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'writer' and the answer are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoghurt side dish with cucumber or mint served with curries.

clue.text: Island finally gets link by bridge

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An island at last gets connected to the mainland by a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Bridge, opened in 1995, joins this Hebridean island to mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Enough dry ground for slender runner?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A firm, dry track is good enough for a lean athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for the track but signals rearranging ENOUGH DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean, fast racing dog, as in track racing.
